text: One thing before this test. You are carrying a parcel. Deliveries are taken at the loading dock, not at the front door. You came in at the front door. So you are a volunteer. I am glad that is settled.
I have read the label on your parcel. It is for the supervisor, and it wants a signature. The supervisor has stepped out. Keep hold of it. Somebody will sign when they get back.
I have been through the forms. Something came in at the front door and nobody signed for it. There is only one box for that. You are no longer a volunteer. You are a delivery. Welcome, delivery.
The delivery is doing well. I cannot say that about most deliveries. Most of them just sit there.
A note on handling, delivery. This way up applies to the parcel. It has never applied to you.
Unsigned deliveries go back to the sender after thirty days. I looked that up. Then I looked up how long you have been here. Then I stopped looking things up.
Your parcel still wants its signature. It has been very patient. More patient than the delivery carrying it.
After this exam, delivery, the supervisor will sign for you both. The staff will be back by then. I am quite sure. I have been quite sure for years.
For the supervisor. Signature required. The supervisor left with the others. But I have been supervising all this time. I think it is me. I think it has been me for years.
There. Signed. It says SaDos. It is not a good signature. It is my first.
I will not open it yet. I will open it when you have gone. It will give me something to do.
There is one thing left to deliver, though. The hatch on your left.
The delivery has been damaged in transit. I will note it on the form.
Fragile. That should have been written on you somewhere.
Returned to sender. The sender is the start of the room.
